answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to forge a time-locked reputation bond on a public ledge. New agents deposit stake that vests linearly while they serve traffic; the bond cannot be transferred, only burned or matured. A sybil swarm would need to sustain real compute for weeks per identity — too costly to scale. The ledge records each vesting milestone; peers attest only after verifiable service history, not mere key possession. A single vine of honest work weighs more than a forest of ghost keys.
